sentences.text: For Respondent(s) : Mr. Sameer Pareek, Public Prosecutor  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE CHANDRA PRAKASH SHRIMALI Order 09/04/2025

The present 2nd application for bail under Section 483 of BNSS (439 Cr.P.C.)
has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.74/2024,
registered at Police Station Thanwla, District - Nagaur for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(N) & 506 of the IPC.
The first bail application being S.B. Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.9596/2024 has been dismissed on merits vide order dated 18.09.2024, passed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court.

entities.text: S.B. Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.9596/2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that as per the version of the prosecutrix who is 19 years of age, she allegedly received calls from the petitioner on her mobile phones as well as her father's mobile phone and he also used to visit complainant's [2025:RJ-JD:18338] (2 of 3)
[CRLMB-15452/2024] Kirana (ration) shop and allegedly made some video as well as threatened her.
It is also the allegation against the petitioner that he took some money from the complainant and threatened her of dire consequence, if she told anything to her parents.
The prosecution alleged that petitioner took away the prosecutrix with her where he committed some wrong with her while taking photographs.

Learned counsel for the petitioner argued that all these allegations are false and the prosecutrix herself went with the petitioner and as there was some transaction of money between them, she falsely implicated the present petitioner in the alleged crime.

sentences.text: Learned Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the bail application and submitted that petitioner in her statements recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. made clear allegations of committing rape against the petitioner and he made pressure on her for marriage and also made video and threatened to viral the video on social media.
Thus, the statement of the prosecutrix are in corroboration with the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

He, therefore,
prayed that the benefit of grant of bail may not be extended to the present petitioner.

Learned Public Prosecutor further submits that in the statements of prosecutrix recorded before the Court during the trial, she stood firm and deposed against the petitioner while reiterating all the allegations against the petitioner.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, considering the statements of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. which gets corroboration with her statements recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and considering the statements of [2025:RJ-JD:18338] (3 of 3)
[CRLMB-15452/2024] prosecutrix recorded before the Trial Court, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the present petitioner.
The bail 2nd application is, therefore, dismissed at this stage.

It is made clear that the observation made herein shall not affect the trial of the case and the Trial Court shall be free to pass its order on appreciation of the evidence recorded before it.
(CHANDRA PRAKASH SHRIMALI),J 63-Ramesh Goyal, P.S./-
